correctness.rationale: Two generating support inequalities show every horizontal polar slice is an explicitly scaled copy of K°; integrating these exact slices proves the polar-volume formula. K being Santaló-centered implies centroid(K°)=0 and therefore the horizontal polar first moments vanish. The axial volume derivative is strictly increasing and its unique zero gives the full Santaló point. A beta-mixture decomposition of frustum heights gives Q(centroid)>0, hence strict Santaló-below-centroid order; the Jensen/envelope argument gives strict monotonicity of the factorized Mahler product. The script independently rebuilds polar polytopes for asymmetric and symmetric bases and checks symbolic and numerical cases.
risks: The finite symbolic and polyhedral checks are diagnostic; they do not prove the all-dimensional theorem or arbitrariness of K.

originality.rationale: Meyer--Reisner prove the exact pyramid endpoint (Lemma 11), and this is explicitly not claimed new. Their full text addresses shadow systems and small-vertex reverse inequalities rather than the nondegenerate homothetic-frustum polar-volume/centroid/Mahler law. Pavlov--Telen establish a general rational-volume framework for Santaló points of polytopes, while Izmestiev gives a projective-center characterization; neither inspected statement supplies the universal closed frustum identity or strict Mahler monotonicity. Searches across equivalent geometric names and explicit formula fingerprints did not locate an implication-equivalent result. The accepted claim is the interior family structure and its strict inequalities.
residual_risks: A previously calculated frustum polar volume could be embedded in older unindexed projective or convex-geometry literature.
General rational-function methods can derive individual polytope cases; this result claims a uniform theorem for every convex base and all dimensions, not general algorithmic solvability.
The pyramid endpoint Santaló formula and product factor are prior-covered and excluded as independent discoveries.
risks: An older unindexed paper or mathematical handbook might contain the same elementary frustum polar-volume calculation.
A general-purpose Santaló polytope algorithm can derive these particular equations after a nontrivial specialization, so algorithmic solvability is not claimed new.

value.rationale: The classical Santaló point and Mahler product are central affine-geometric invariants, and a two-homothetic-face frustum is a natural continuous deformation of the published pyramid class into a prism. Exact Santaló points are rarely base-independent for general convex shapes. The theorem gives one universal exact polar and product law in every dimension, strict separation from the ordinary centroid, and strict monotone interpolation of the volume product, not merely an endpoint recomputation.
risks: The theorem is confined to homothetic frusta and does not solve the unrelated general skew-prismatoid Santaló problem.
